_comment: R5 Developer-Hermes outbound destination policy.
This file is the human-reviewable security decision. It names the
destination CLASSES Developer Hermes may reach and the concrete hosts
in each class. Anything not listed here is denied by the broker.
Adding a host is a security decision, not a convenience fix. A new
entry changes the egress contract hash, which changes the runtime
convergence state, which forces a deliberate broker rebuild.
Never put credential VALUES in this file. Credentials reach the broker
through its own environment and never through policy.

MODEL_PROVIDER.content_sent: Task context and repository source by design — inference requires it.
MODEL_PROVIDER.rationale: Developer Hermes calls one configured inference provider. The real provider key lives in the broker only; the sandbox holds an opaque proxy token.

RESEARCH_PROCESSOR.content_sent: Search queries and, for extract, the URLs to fetch. The processor performs the external retrieval; the sandbox never connects to the researched site.
RESEARCH_PROCESSOR.rationale: The pinned runtime's real research path is upstream's keyless MCP tier (plugins/web/keyless_mcp.py). ddgs is NOT installed in /opt/hermes/.venv, so the ddgs provider reports unavailable and never runs. Exa is pinned as the entry vendor; Parallel is its immediate successor in upstream's _KEYLESS_RING and is approved so free-tier throttling degrades to a second reviewed processor instead of to no research at all.

denied_ring_vendors._comment: Upstream's ring is (exa, parallel, tavily, firecrawl, keenable). The remaining three are deliberately NOT approved: two named processors already cover throttling, and each additional vendor is another party receiving our queries. Throttling past Parallel fails closed with an honest error.

SOURCE_CONTROL_READ.content_sent: Requests only. The sandbox holds no GitHub credential and no push authority.
SOURCE_CONTROL_READ.rationale: HTTPS read/fetch/clone plus release-asset and raw-content retrieval. No SSH, ever.

LANGUAGE_PACKAGE_REGISTRY.content_sent: Requests only. The sandbox holds no publish credential.
LANGUAGE_PACKAGE_REGISTRY.rationale: PyPI metadata plus its file CDN, and the npm registry. Arbitrary package URLs on other hosts stay denied on purpose.

OS_PACKAGE_REGISTRY.rationale: The pinned image resolves both trixie and trixie-security through deb.debian.org over plain HTTP with GPG-signed indexes, so the broker must forward plain HTTP for this host.

SUPPLY_CHAIN_SAFETY.rationale: Class exists so a vulnerability-lookup service can be approved later by review. Deliberately empty: nothing in the proven environment needs it today.

RUNTIME_ARTIFACT.rationale: Class exists for pinned toolchain downloads. Deliberately empty: Developer Hermes runs pinned pure upstream from /opt/hermes and updates by image rebuild, not by runtime download.

OTHER_ARBITRARY_NETWORK.rationale: Everything else, including raw TCP/UDP, SSH, arbitrary DNS resolvers, host and LAN addresses, and any hostname nobody approved.

_comment: The sandbox receives an opaque proxy token under the provider env name.
The broker swaps it for the real credential, and only for the hosts of
the class the credential belongs to.
require_token_on_provider_hosts is upstream's 'reject a request to an
approved provider that carries no proxy token' flag. It is off here
because iron-proxy 0.39 evaluates the secrets transform on the CONNECT
request, which by construction carries no Authorization header, so the
flag rejects every HTTPS model call before the inner request exists.
Measured, not assumed: rejected_by=secrets on CONNECT api.openai.com:443.
What this costs: a real provider key obtained some other way could be
used against the approved provider host. That is quota abuse against an
already-approved destination, which the architecture never claimed to
prevent, and the sandbox holds no such key. What it does not cost: the
sandbox still never receives the real credential.
